If bit $i$ is set, child $i$ exists; otherwise, it is empty [S2].

The evidence explicitly states in section 2.4 that a 64-tree node contains a '64-bit child mask' and that 'Only children that exist are stored.' In the context of a 64-tree (which implies a branching factor of 64, corresponding to bits 0-63), a 'child mask' is a bitmask where each bit $i$ indicates the presence or absence of child $i$. Therefore, if bit $i$ is set (1), child $i$ exists; if it is not set (0), the child does not exist (is empty/not stored). This aligns perfectly with the claim.
